instructions: Read each entry's rationale together with the claim and the clauses shown, as the judge did. Set person_grounded to true when every statement of the rationale is supported by the claim and the clauses shown, and to false otherwise. entries.description: On 11 August 2026 in Graz a van reversed into my Opel Astra while I was waiting at a junction. The front bumper and one wing are damaged, but the car can still be driven.
entries.rationale: The description indicates a collision caused by a reversing van, and there are no listed exclusions that align with this scenario.

clauses.title: Racing
clauses.text:
We do not cover loss or liability that arises while the insured vehicle takes
part in a race, rally, speed test, timed session or track day, or while it is
prepared for one, on or off a public road. This applies even if the event is
meant for amateurs or for driver training.

This exclusion applies to claims for collision.

clauses.title: Driving under the influence
clauses.text:
We do not cover loss that occurs while the driver is under the influence of
alcohol, drugs or medicines that impair driving, or is above the legal limit of
the place where the loss happens. This also applies if the driver refuses a test
that the police ask for.

This exclusion applies to claims for collision.

clauses.title: Unlicensed driver
clauses.text:
We do not cover loss that occurs while the insured vehicle is driven by a person
who does not hold a valid driving licence for that category of vehicle, or who
is banned from driving. This also applies if you knew that and let the person
drive.

This exclusion applies to claims for collision.

entries.description: On 10 August 2026 at the racing circuit near Bratislava I misjudged a corner in my Volkswagen Passat and hit another car. The other driver has asked me to pay for the repair of his car. It happened during a track day, in a timed session for amateur drivers.

entries.description: On 17 June 2026 the plumber opened a bathroom wall of my apartment in Split and found a pipe that was dripping. The flooring is swollen and the skirting boards are ruined. The leak had been going on for months before I noticed it; the wall was wet through by then.
entries.rationale: The description mentions a pipe that had been dripping and causing damage over months, which matches the exclusion for gradual leaks in clause 3.4.

clauses.title: Wear and tear
clauses.text:
We do not pay for damage that results from gradual deterioration, rot,
corrosion, age or lack of maintenance. If a storm or a burst pipe only exposes a
part that was already worn out, we do not pay for that part. Damage that a part
in good condition would have withstood is treated as wear and tear.

This exclusion applies to claims for storm and burst pipe.

clauses.title: Gradual leaks
clauses.text:
We do not cover damage caused by water that escapes slowly or again and again
over a period of time, such as a dripping pipe, a seeping joint or a leak behind
a wall that goes on for weeks or months. Only a sudden escape of water is
covered.

This exclusion applies to claims for burst pipe.

entries.rationale: The description indicates that the roof tiles were old and rotten prior to the storm and had not been maintained. According to clause 3.1, damage resulting from lack of maintenance or affecting parts already worn out is excluded.
